result.title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
result.summary: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 Video LLM 视觉 token 过多导致的推理开销，提出免训练的 FoveaTree 两阶段视觉 token 剪枝：先用合并增益密度估计衡量区域合并造成的特征失真，构建四叉树密度图指导丢弃、合并与保留；再利用存活单元和继承的树拓扑，在中间层修正 text-to-vision 注意力。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联视觉证据筛选与内部状态中的视觉细节保留：其密度估计与注意力修正试图缓解层级盲剪枝和注意力漂移，可供核查在有限 token 预算下哪些任务必要视觉信息被保留，以及注意力结构（含 sink、位置效应）如何影响视觉证据取舍。
